messages.content: Write a short story.

Max was a lonely little boy. He wanted to go outside and play but he was scared. He sat on his room, feeling sad.

His mom came to him and said "I want to spoil you, Max! I've got something special for you!" Max was so excited.

His mom went away and came back with a big, shining box. Inside the box was a big bar of soap. Max was so happy! He had never seen soap like this before. 

Max's mom took him outside and let him play in the garden. He was so happy and he decided to use the soap to make bubbles. He watched the bubbles and laughed.

Max knew that he was never lonely with his mom and the special soap. From then on, Max always felt happy and spoilt!
Write a short story.

John was so embarrassed. He had just gone to a concert where he had seen his favorite singer, and he thought it was the best thing ever. He had been singing and dancing along, but when he looked up, he saw a huge fan right in front of him. 

"What are you doing up here?" the fan asked in surprise.

John felt so embarrassed, he couldn't answer.

The fan smiled. "It's ok. I'm glad you like the singer so much. You must be a huge fan!" 

John nodded. He wasn't embarrassed anymore and he started to smile too.
Write a short story.

Dave was going on a walk to the park. He saw a small bird that was chirping and singing in a tree. Suddenly, the bird started to scatter its feathers everywhere. 
Dave was happy and started laughing. He thought it was so hilarious to see the feathers flying. Then he noticed something else in the sky. It was a harmless dragonfly. 
Dave was excited and followed after it. He watched it buzz and flutter away until it was gone. 
Dave began to think about how things were different from his opinion. He thought it was so cool how something as harmless as a dragonfly could be so colorful and beautiful. 
He quickly ran back home feeling inspired from his adventure and started to draw a picture of the dragonfly he saw.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to jump up and down on his bed. One day, he jumped so high that he accidentally broke his bed. 

Timmy's mom came into his room and saw the broken bed. "Oh no, Timmy! Your bed is broken," she said. 

Timmy felt sad because he loved his bed. "Can you fix it, Mommy?" he asked. 

His mom smiled and said, "Of course, but while I fix your bed, why don't you play your drum?" Timmy loved playing his drum, so he happily started playing while his mom fixed his bed.
Write a short story.

Lily loved to draw with her pen. She liked to make pictures of flowers, stars, and animals. She had a big book of paper where she kept all her drawings. She was very proud of them.

One day, she saw a new pen on the table. It was shiny and red, and it had a button on the side. Lily was curious. She wanted to try the new pen. She picked it up and pressed the button. A bright green light came out of the tip. Lily was amazed. She thought it was a magic pen.

She ran to her book of paper and started to draw with the green light. She made a big circle, a triangle, and a smiley face. She giggled and pressed the button again. The light changed to blue. She drew a fish, a cloud, and a heart. She pressed the button again and again, and the light changed to different colors. She drew a rainbow, a sun, and a flower. She was having so much fun.

She did not hear her mom come into the room. Her mom saw the new pen in Lily's hand and the colorful drawings on the paper. She was angry. She said, "Lily, what are you doing? That is not your pen. That is daddy's pen. He needs it for his work. You are not supposed to touch it. You have ruined his paper. How could you be so naughty?"

Lily was scared. She dropped the pen and looked at her mom. She felt guilty. She knew she had done something bad. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to try the pen. It was so pretty and fun. I didn't mean to ruin daddy's paper. Please don't be mad at me."

Her mom sighed. She gazed at Lily and saw her sad face. She felt sorry for her. She said, "I know you didn't mean to, Lily. But you have to ask before you use something that is not yours. And you have to be careful with things that are important to other people. Daddy will be very upset when he sees his paper. You have to say sorry to him and help him fix it. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "I understand, mom. I'm sorry. I love you. I love daddy. I will say sorry to him and help him fix it. Can I still draw with my pen?"

Her mom smiled. She said, "Yes, you can still draw with your pen. But only on your own paper. And only with your own colors. OK?"

Lily hugged her mom. She said, "OK, mom. Thank you. You are the best mom ever."
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to wear his favorite hat every day. One day, it started to rain and Timmy's hat got wet. He didn't like his hat when it was wet, he wanted it to be dry again. 

Timmy's mom put the hat in the dryer to make it dry. Timmy was happy when he got his hat back because it was dry again. He put it on his head and went outside to play. 

While he was playing, Timmy saw a flower that needed water. He took his hat off and used it to yield water from a nearby puddle. The flower was happy and Timmy was happy too because he was able to help the flower.
Write a short story.

Ben and Lily were twins. They liked to play with cards. They had many cards with animals and colors. They enjoyed making pairs and matching them.

One day, they found a new card in their box. It was a big card with a funny face. It had a red nose, a green hat and a yellow smile. Ben and Lily did not know what it was.

"Look, Lily, what is this?" Ben asked.

"I don't know, Ben. Maybe it is a clown," Lily said.

"A clown? What is a clown?" Ben wondered.

"A clown is a person who makes jokes and laughs. They wear silly clothes and make-up. They are in the circus," Lily explained.

"Oh, I see. Do you want to play with the clown card?" Ben asked.

"Sure, Ben. Let's play. Maybe we can make jokes too," Lily agreed.

They took the clown card and pretended to be clowns. They put the card on their nose, on their hat and on their mouth. They made funny noises and faces. They laughed and laughed.

They enjoyed playing with the clown card. They did not know that the card was a joker. A joker is a card that is not part of the game. It is a card that is used to trick people. It is a foolish card.

But Ben and Lily did not care. They had fun with the foolish card. They were happy clowns.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl named Jane. Jane had a special cane that she enjoyed playing with. Every day, Jane would take her cane and go for a walk. She loved feeling the sun on her back and the wind in her hair. 

One day, Jane came across a park with some cute animals. She saw rabbits hopping around, and birds flying in the sky. She also found a pond filled with beautiful fish. Jane was so excited that she began running and swinging her cane around. 

After she had explored the park, Jane sat down on the grass and happily munched away on some snacks. Her cane was lying beside her, and Jane enjoyed the peace and tranquillity of the spot she had found. 

The time when Jane visited the park was one of her happiest memories. She enjoyed every minute, and would often think back to that special day.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. Jane lived with her mom and dad. One day, her mom made some dough for baking a cake. Jane wanted to help so her mom gave her the dough and said, "Roll the dough very carefully, Jane." 

Jane started to roll the dough, but all of a sudden she reversed and rolled it the other way. She thought it looked more fun that way. But when she showed it to her mom, her mom said, "That's not right, Jane. You need to roll it one way or else the cake won't come out the way it should."

Jane didn't want to do it the right way so she continued to roll the dough the wrong way. Her mom got very uncomfortable with this and shouted, "Jane, reverse the dough now!" 

Jane looked at her mom and knew she had to do it. She slowly began reversing the dough and finally, it was rolled the right way. Her mom smiled and said, "That was much better, Jane." 

From then on Jane made sure to always roll the dough the right way.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, in a big brown house, there was a long hall. In this hall, there were two toys, a bear and a robot. They lived in the brown house with a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with the bear and the robot every day.

One day, the bear and the robot had a fight in the hall. They were fighting over a big red ball that Tim liked to play with. The bear wanted to play with the ball, but so did the robot. They both wanted the ball very much.

Tim heard the noise and came to the hall. He saw the bear and the robot fighting. Tim said, "Stop fighting! We can all play with the ball together." The bear and the robot stopped fighting and listened to Tim. They all played with the big red ball in the hall and had lots of fun. From that day on, the bear and the robot learned to share and play together.
Write a short story.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy cars in the living room. They liked to make them zoom and crash on the carpet. Lily had a red car and Ben had a blue car. They pretended they were racing on a big road.

"Vroom, vroom, I'm faster than you!" Lily said.

"No, you're not, I'm faster!" Ben said.

They pushed their cars harder and harder, until they reached the sofa. Lily's car hit the sofa leg and bounced back. Ben's car hit Lily's car and made a loud noise.

"Hey, you wrecked my car!" Lily cried.

"No, you wrecked mine!" Ben shouted.

They both grabbed their cars and looked at them. They had scratches and dents on them. They were not shiny and smooth anymore.

Lily and Ben were very sad and angry. They glared at each other and started to yell.

"Give me your car, it's better than mine!" Lily demanded.

"No, give me your car, it's better than yours!" Ben demanded.

They pulled and tugged at each other's cars, trying to take them away. They were both strong, but they could not win.

"Stop it, stop it, you two!" Mom said. She heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily and Ben fighting over their cars. She was not happy.

"Let go of the cars, now!" Mom said. She took the cars from their hands and put them on the table. She looked at them and shook her head.

"Look what you did, you wrecked your cars. You were not careful and gentle with them. You were not nice and kind to each other. You should be sorry and say sorry," Mom said.

Lily and Ben looked at their cars and felt bad. They knew Mom was right. They did not want to wreck their cars. They did not want to fight with each other. They wanted to play and have fun.

They looked at each other and lowered their heads.

"Sorry, Lily," Ben said.

"Sorry, Ben," Lily said.

They hugged each other and smiled.

Mom smiled too. She was glad they said sorry. She gave them their cars back and kissed them.

"Good, now you can play again. But be careful and gentle with your cars. And be nice and kind to each other. You are both strong, but you are also sweet," Mom said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They thanked Mom and took their cars. They went back to the carpet and played. They did not zoom and crash anymore. They drove and parked and talked.

"Your car is nice, Lily," Ben said.

"Your car is nice, Ben," Lily said.

They were happy and friendly. They shared and cared. They had fun.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a generous girl named Amy. She decided to go to the park with her two favorite things- her waffle and her teddy bear. 

When she got to the park, Amy saw a little boy. He was playing with a toy car. "Hi there," Amy said.

The little boy looked up. "What do you have?" 

Amy held up her waffle. "This is my waffle. Would you like to have some?"

The little boy's eyes sparkled. "Yes please!"

So Amy shared her waffle with the little boy. They both ate it and laughed together. Amy was so generous, she gave the little boy the rest of the waffle to take home. 

The little boy thanked Amy and ran off playing with his toy car. Amy smiled and waved goodbye as she left the park.
Write a short story.

Once, there was a man who had an expensive van. He drove it everywhere and never wanted to let it go.

One day, the man was driving it and he heard a noise. He stopped to take a look and he saw the engine was broken! He was very sad.

He couldn't afford to fix it so he threw the van away. Everyone was sad, but was happy that the van was gone.

The man decided that he no longer needed a van. And he promised himself he would never buy an expensive van again.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she found a shiny penny made of copper on the ground. She picked it up and put it in her pocket, feeling proud of her treasure.

As she walked along, she saw a small bird with a broken wing. The bird looked sad and scared. Lily knew she had to help the bird, so she carefully picked it up and carried it in her hands. She didn't know what to do, but she knew she couldn't leave the bird alone.

Lily took the bird to her mother, who helped her find a wildlife rescue center. The people at the center were able to fix the bird's wing and release it back into the wild. Lily felt happy that she had helped the bird, even though it was an unknown creature to her. She learned that sometimes, helping others can bring joy and happiness to both the giver and the receiver.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little girl named Gabby. Gabby loved to build things with her blocks. One day, she had a great idea. She wanted to build a new bathrobe! She grabbed her blocks and she started building. She put the blocks together, one by one. She built and built until she had built a bathrobe! It was the best bathrobe she had ever seen! She put it on and she ran around the house. Everyone laughed at how funny it looked. From that day forward, Gabby always wore her special bathrobe.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was very adventurous and he loved to explore. One day, Timmy went to the beach with his mom. They played in the sand and swam in the water. Suddenly, Timmy saw a shark in the water! 

"Mommy, look! A shark!" Timmy shouted. 

"Don't worry, Timmy. Sharks are friendly. They just want to swim," said his mom. 

But Timmy was scared. He didn't want to swim anymore. "Mommy, can we stand on the sand instead?" he asked. 

"Of course, Timmy. We can stand and watch the shark swim," said his mom. And so, they stood on the sand and watched the shark swim in the water. Timmy was still scared, but he felt safe standing on the sand with his mom.
Write a short story.

Kitty was a very happy and curious cat. She often liked to explore the world around her and discover new things. Kitty was always so eager to learn and gain more knowledge about her environment.

One day, Kitty was playing in the garden and she noticed a small patch of vegetables. She had seen it before but now it was much bigger than before. Kitty was excited. She wanted to discover what was in the patch so she ran to it.

In the patch, the troubled Kitty found that the vegetables had been stepped on and the plants were broken. She was so sad that someone had hurt this patch and she didn't think it would ever be the same again.

Kitty decided to help the garden and so she did her best to fix the vegetables. Over time, the garden started to become beautiful once more and Kitty could see the fruits of her labour.

All the work had paid off. Kitty was happy and relieved. She was proud of what she had achieved yet she still felt troubled that someone had hurt the garden before. But Kitty was determined to take care of the garden and make it even better than it had been before.
Write a short story.

Once there was a girl named Molly. She liked to be very silly and she liked to wear bright colours. Today she decided to wear her prettiest dress. It was bright pink with lots of ribbons.

Molly went out to the street to get the mail. But today something strange happened. There was a big dog in the mailbox. He was so shy he wouldn't come out. Molly tried to coax him away but he wouldn't budge.

Molly didn't know what to do. Then she had an idea. She slowly pulled something out from her pocket. "Do you like cookies?" she asked in a gentle voice.
The dog slowly walked out from the mailbox. He happily ate the cookie Molly offered him. Molly smiled, happy that the dog was finally safe.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time there was a deaf vendor. He sold yummy treats like ice cream and candy to lots of people. Everyone loved the vendor, but he had a problem. He could not hear the customers and they could not hear him.

The vendor wanted to succeed. He tried many things to help him hear and talk with people. Nothing worked. He was sad, but he kept trying.

One day, he saw something that made him happy. The vendor had a big smile on his face!

The vendor found a special machine. The machine could help him hear what people said. He bought the machine and it worked! The vendor could now hear and talk to people.

Finally, he had succeeded! He was so happy and everyone was happy for him. Now people could understand the vendor and he could understand them. Everyone loved the vendor even more.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Tom and Jack. Tom was envious of Jack's plan to take a taxi to the beach. He wished he could join him.

Tom said, "Jack, can I also go with you on the taxi ride?"
Jack shook his head and said, "No, I'm sorry Tom. I plan to go alone."

Tom was sad and envious. He wanted to go on a taxi ride too. He thought, "Maybe I can plan to take a taxi on my own!"

So, Tom asked his mom if he could take a taxi to the beach. His mom said, "Of course, you can take a taxi. Just remember to always be safe."

Tom was so excited. He quickly said goodbye to Jack and ran to the taxi. He enjoyed his taxi ride to the beach and had lots of fun.

When the day was over, Tom and Jack compared stories. Tom said, "I'm so glad I planned to take a taxi. I had the best day ever!" Jack was still a little envious, but happy for his best friend.
Write a short story.

One day, Jack and his family went to the park. Jack couldn't wait to explore the huge playground. His mum said, "Let's spend the day here, Jack. It will be quick and easy."

Jack grinned and started running around. He found the swings and he spent a long time on them. He raced around the slides, and then he came across a sandpit.

Jack loved digging in the sand, and quickly filled a bucket with sand. But then he noticed a strange animal in the sand. It had big eyes, and was fast and quick.

At first, Jack was scared. But then he saw that the animal was friendly. He scooped it out of the sand and spent the rest of the day playing with it.

Jack and the animal were fast friends. His mum couldn't believe it when she saw them together. "It's amazing how easy it was," she said. Jack smiled, happy with his new found friend.
Write a short story.

Ben likes to sign. He signs hello, thank you, and sorry. He signs when he is happy, sad, or angry. He signs to his mom, his dad, and his dog. He signs a lot.

One day, Ben goes to the lab with his mom. His mom works in the lab. She helps sick people. She wears a white coat and a mask. She looks at small things in big machines. Ben thinks the lab is fun.

But the lab is not for signing. The lab is for being quiet and careful. Ben's mom tells him to sit and wait. She gives him a book and a toy. She says she will be back soon.

Ben tries to sit and wait. But he is bored. He does not like the book or the toy. He wants to sign. He sees a man in a white coat and a mask. He signs hello to him. The man does not see him. He sees a woman in a white coat and a mask. He signs thank you to her. The woman does not hear him. He sees a cat in a cage. He signs sorry to it. The cat does not care.

Ben is persistent. He does not give up. He signs to everyone and everything in the lab. He makes a lot of noise. He makes a lot of mess. He makes a lot of trouble.

Ben's mom comes back. She sees Ben signing. She sees the noise, the mess, and the trouble. She is not happy. She is angry. She signs sorry to the man, the woman, and the cat. She signs no to Ben. She takes him out of the lab. She says he cannot come back.

Ben is sad. He likes to sign. He likes the lab. He does not like to make his mom angry. He signs sorry to his mom. He signs he loves her. His mom signs sorry to him. She signs she loves him. She says he can sign at home. She says he can sign with his dad and his dog. She says he can sign with her when she is not in the lab.

Ben is happy. He signs okay to his mom. He signs he understands. He signs he will be quiet and careful in the lab. He signs he will wait for her. He signs he is proud of her. His mom signs okay to him. She signs she is proud of him. She signs he is a good boy. She signs he is a smart boy. She signs he is a special boy. She signs he is her boy.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Tim who lived in the city. He had the best tutor ever, who showed him amazing things. One day, the tutor showed him something even more amazing. It was a big box with a lock on it! Tim was so excited and wanted to open the box. So, he asked his tutor how to unlock it. The tutor smiled, took a key from his pocket, and put it into the lock. Then, as Tim watched, he unlocked the box. The box opened and out came the most amazing sight Tim had ever seen. It was a robot! Tim was amazed!
Write a short story.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big gate with a lock. They want to know what is behind the gate.

"Can we go there?" Lila asks Ben.

"I don't know. Maybe it is not safe. Maybe it is not for us." Ben says.

"But it looks fun. Maybe there is a slide or a swing or a sandbox." Lila says.

They look around. They do not see any grown-ups. They do not see any signs. They only see the gate and the lock.

"Let's try to open it." Lila says. She pulls the lock. It does not move. She pushes the lock. It does not move. She shakes the lock. It does not move.

"It is too hard. We need a key." Ben says.

"Where can we find a key?" Lila says.

They look around again. They see a small house near the gate. It has a window and a door. The window is bright. The door is dark.

"Maybe there is a key in the house." Ben says.

"Let's go and see." Lila says.

They run to the house. They knock on the door. No one answers. They try to open the door. It is not locked. They go inside.

The house is small and cozy. It has a sofa, a table, a chair, a lamp, and a shelf. On the shelf, they see many things. They see books, toys, pictures, and a key.

"Look, there is the key!" Lila says. She points to the key. It is shiny and silver.

"Let's take it and open the gate." Ben says.

They grab the key and run to the gate. They put the key in the lock. They turn the key. The lock clicks. The gate opens.

They are happy. They go through the gate. They see a big garden. It has flowers, trees, birds, and butterflies. It is beautiful.

"Wow, this is amazing!" Lila says.

"Yes, it is. Let's play here." Ben says.

They play in the garden. They smell the flowers. They climb the trees. They chase the birds. They catch the butterflies. They have fun.

They do not hear the voice. The voice is angry. The voice is loud.

"Hey, you two! What are you doing here? This is my garden. You are not permitted to be here. Give me back my key. Now!" The voice says.

They turn around. They see a man. He is old and grumpy. He is the owner of the house and the garden. He is not happy. He is mad.

They are scared. They drop the key. They run to the gate. They go through the gate. They close the gate. They lock the gate. They run to the park.

They do not play in the park. They do not talk to each other. They are sorry. They are sad.

They learned a lesson. They learned to respect other people's things. They learned to ask for permission. They learned to be careful. They learned to be good.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a fisherman. He went out on the lake every day to catch fish. One day, the fisherman noticed something strange. He saw a mermaid in the lake.

The mermaid spoke to the fisherman. She said, â€œI demand that you give me some of the fish you catch today.â€ The fisherman was surprised. He didnâ€™t want to give away any of his fish.

So, the fisherman asked the mermaid, â€œWhy do you want the fish?â€ The mermaid said, â€œIâ€™m hungry. Please give me some of your fish!â€

The fisherman felt guilty. He said, â€œOkay, I will give you some of the fish.â€ So he gave the mermaid half of the fish he had caught that day. 

The mermaid thanked the fisherman and swam away. The fisherman went home feeling happy that he had done something kind.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time there was a girl. Her name was Lucy and she was three years old. Every day, Lucy and her mummy would take a walk in the countryside. She loved exploring and finding new things on their walks. 

One day, Lucy found a puzzle on their walk. She was so excited and asked her mum if she could take it home and finish it. Her mummy said yes and she took it home. 

Lucy worked really hard on the puzzle, even when it felt difficult. Finally she finished the puzzle and her mum was very proud of her. 

As a reward, Lucy's mum gave her a toy surprise. Lucy was so happy and couldn't believe she had finished the puzzle. She smiled a big smile and was proud of herself. 

The End.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a helpful girl named Lily. She loved to draw with chalk on the sidewalk. One sunny day, Lily was drawing a big, happy sun with her yellow chalk.

Lily's mom called her to come inside and eat lunch. Lily did not want to delay, but she also did not want to stop drawing. So, she asked her mom if she could finish her drawing first. Her mom said yes, but only if she came inside right after.

Lily finished her sun and went inside to eat her lunch. She was happy that she could be helpful and listen to her mom. After lunch, Lily went back outside to draw more with her chalk. She was a good girl who knew when to delay and when to be helpful.
Write a short story.

Once there was a little girl who had a bad towel. It wasn't soft or fluffy, it was rough and scratchy. The little girl was very sad. She asked herself, "Why is my towel so bad?"

The little girl asked her mom why her towel was so bad. Her mom said, "That towel is old, it needs to be replaced." The little girl didn't understand what it meant to be replaced, so she asked her mom to explain.

Her mom said, "A new towel will be soft and fluffy. It won't feel bad like this one." The little girl smiled and asked where she could get a new towel.

Her mom said, "It's easy, just go to the store and pick out a new one!" The little girl was so happy. She thanked her mom, put on her shoes, and went off to the store. 

When she got there, she looked at all the different towels. After some careful thinking, she chose a big, bright, fluffy towel. She was so happy!

When she got home, she put the new towel to the test. She ran it under water and rubbed it on her skin. It was soft and fluffy - just like her mom promised. She never had to wonder why her towel was so bad ever again!
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Floppy. Floppy was very adorable with soft fur and floppy ears. Floppy loved to jump and play all day long.

One day, Floppy saw a big, scary cat. The cat wanted to eat Floppy for lunch! Floppy was so scared, he didn't know what to do. But then he remembered how much he loved life and how much he loved to jump.

So, Floppy took a deep breath and jumped as high as he could. He jumped over the cat and ran away as fast as he could. Floppy was so happy to be alive and grateful for his jumping skills.

From that day on, Floppy made sure to always be careful and aware of his surroundings. But he never stopped jumping and playing because that was what made his life so much fun.
Write a short story.

Sara and Tom like to play in the big closet. They find many things to wear and pretend. One day, they see a shiny hanger on the top shelf. Sara wants to reach it, but Tom says no. He says it is not for playing. It is for mommy's dress.

But Sara does not listen. She is naughty. She climbs on a box and grabs the hanger. She pulls it hard. But the hanger is stuck. It does not come down. Sara pulls harder. Then, something bad happens. The hanger breaks. And mommy's dress falls down. It is torn and dirty.

Sara and Tom hear mommy coming. They are scared. They enter the closet and hide behind the coats. They hope mommy will not find them. But mommy sees the mess. She sees the broken hanger and the ruined dress. She is angry. She opens the closet and finds Sara and Tom. She scolds them. She says they are very naughty. She says they have to say sorry and help clean up. Sara and Tom feel sorry. They say sorry and help mommy. They learn not to touch things that are not theirs. They learn to be good.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a big truck. The truck was red and had four wheels. It was a vehicle that could carry lots of things. One day, the truck went on a long journey to a distant land. The driver drove for hours and hours until he got very tired. He stopped the truck and decided to take a nap. 

As he slept, the clouds in the sky became dark and grey. Suddenly, it started to rain very heavily. The driver woke up and realized that he had left the back of the truck open. He quickly got out of the truck and ran to cover the things inside with a tarp. He didn't want the rain to ruin anything. 

After he finished covering everything, the driver got back into the truck and continued his journey. He was happy that he had remembered to cover everything and that nothing got wet. Finally, after many hours of driving, he arrived at his destination in the distant land.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim always wore his favorite uniform. It was blue and made him feel special. One day, he saw a big red ball up high in a tree. He wanted to play with it, but it was too high for him to reach.

Tim asked his friend, Sam, for help. "Sam, can you help me reach the ball in the tree?" Sam was taller than Tim. Sam tried to reach the ball, but he couldn't get it either. They both felt a little stupid for not being able to get the ball down.

Then, they had an idea. They found a long stick and used it to poke the ball. The ball fell down from the tree, and they caught it. Tim and Sam were so happy to play with the big red ball together. They learned that sometimes, they need a little help from friends to reach what they want.

Once upon a time, there was a big, green field with lots of trees and flowers. It was called a landscape. A wise owl lived in a tree in the landscape. One day, a little girl came to play in the field. She had a sandwich and some juice. She sat down and ate her lunch, but then she accidentally spilled some juice on her shirt. She needed to wipe it off. The wise owl saw her and flew down to help. He showed her how to use a napkin to wipe the juice away. The little girl was happy and said thank you to the wise owl.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends, but one day she woke up feeling dizzy. Her mom measured her temperature and found out she had a fever.

Lily's mom told her to rest and drink lots of water. Lily was sad she couldn't go outside and play, but she listened to her mom and stayed in bed. Later that day, her mom brought her a surprise - a new book to read!

Lily loved the book and read it all day. When she woke up the next morning, she felt much better. She was so happy she could play with her friends again. She remembered how her mom took care of her and made her feel better. From that day on, Lily made sure to drink lots of water and rest when she felt dizzy.

One day, Jake's mommy wanted to teach him something special. She brought out a model car and explained how it worked. She taught Jake each part and how to move them. He was so excited to learn.

Later that day, Jake wanted to show his mommy what he had learned. But the car wouldn't move. Jake felt sad and wanted to give up.

His mommy saw how discouraged he was. She told him not to worry, and taught him how to fix the car. Jake tried and tried, and eventually it started working. He was so happy!

Jake's mommy was also happy to have been able to teach her son something new. She hugged him and told him she was proud of him. Jake smiled and hugged her back.

Once upon a time there was a kitten named Sophie. Sophie was very patient and gentle, just like all cats are. One day, Sophie went to the veterinarian to get a checkup. She was feeling a little bit sick and she wanted to know why.

The veterinarian took a look at Sophie and everything seemed fine. But then, something terrible happened. Sophie let out a big roar! The veterinarian was shocked and scared.

He said to Sophie, "What's wrong? What's the matter?" Sophie just kept roaring and roaring.

The veterinarian realized that something was very wrong. He tried to calm Sophie down, but nothing he did worked. In the end, he said, "I'm sorry, but I'm afraid Sophie is very, very sick."

Sophie stopped roaring. Everyone in the room was sad. They all said goodbye to Sophie and wished her well. Sadly, Sophie never recovered and her life ended there.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to buy a pretty pigeon. She asked her mom, "Can I buy a pretty pigeon?" Her mom said, "Yes, you can."

The girl was very excited. She ran to the pet store to pick out a pigeon. She looked around and saw so many pigeons. But she wanted the pretty one.

She asked the store owner, pointing to a pretty white pigeon, "Can I buy that one?" The store owner said, "Yes, you can."

The little girl was so happy! She bought the pigeon and took it home. She named the pigeon 'Fluffy' and she took very good care of it. Every day she would take it outside to play. They became best friends. 

The little girl was always so happy when she was with her pretty little pigeon, Fluffy.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named David. He was three years old and he loved music. Every night before he went to bed, he liked to perform.

One night, he decided to play a new song. He had never heard it before, but knew he could do it. He plucked each note carefully and slowly. After a few minutes, the song started to sound really nice.

But then something strange happened. The notes suddenly became dull and monotonous. David tried to play it again but it just wouldn't sound right. He stopped playing the song and looked around. What had happened?

Then, he saw it. A big bug was sitting on the strings. When he tried to play the notes, the bug would jump onto other strings, making them dull.

David shook his head in disbelief. The bug had ruined his song. He looked around for something to brush it away with, but couldn't find anything.

So, David waited and watched. After a few minutes, the bug flew away and David was able to continue playing his song. The notes were back to sounding clear and beautiful.

David was happy and he smiled to himself. He enjoyed performing the rest of the song and went to sleep feeling proud of himself.
Write a short story.

Molly was a clumsy girl. She had big feet, and often she stumbled and bumped into things.

One day, Molly was out in the garden. There was silence all around. She was about to go inside when she heard a noise. It was a noise she had never heard before.

The noise was getting closer and closer. Molly's heart was racing. She was feeling scared.

Then, the noise stopped. Molly looked around the corner to see what it was.

It was a furry little puppy! It was scared too, so Molly bent down and slowly held out her hand. The little puppy came closer and closer until it was right next to her.

Molly smiled with delight - the puppy was hers! She picked it up and cuddled it close. From that day on, the puppy and Molly were the best of friends.
Write a short story.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play with paper. They cut paper, fold paper, and draw on paper. They make paper hats, paper planes, and paper animals.

One day, they find a big paper in the park. It is white and clean. They are happy. They want to make something with it.

"What do you want to make?" Tom asks Sue.

"I want to make a paper castle," Sue says. "It will be mighty and pretty."

"OK, let's make a paper castle," Tom says. "I will help you."

They start to cut and fold the paper. They make paper walls, paper towers, and paper flags. They work hard and have fun.

But then, a big wind comes. It blows the paper castle away. It flies high in the sky. Tom and Sue are sad. They worry. They want their paper castle back.

"Where is our paper castle?" Tom cries.

"I don't know," Sue says. "Maybe it is gone forever."

They look at the sky. They hope to see their paper castle. But they only see clouds and birds.

They feel bad. They sit on the grass. They do not play anymore.

Then, they hear a voice. It is a man. He is holding their paper castle. He is smiling.

"Hello, children," he says. "Is this your paper castle? I found it on the other side of the park. It is mighty and pretty. Do you want it back?"

Tom and Sue are happy. They jump and clap. They thank the man. They take their paper castle.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you," they say.

"You're welcome, you're welcome, you're welcome," the man says. "Have fun with your paper castle. But be careful with the wind."

Tom and Sue nod. They hug their paper castle. They are not sad or worry anymore. They are happy and proud. They have their paper castle back. They play with it again. They are friends.
Write a short story.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat oats for breakfast. Every morning, his mom would give him a big bowl of warm oats to make him strong, because he was a weak little boy.

One day, Tim saw a small bird outside his window. The bird was weak too and couldn't fly. Tim wanted to help the bird. He thought, "Maybe the bird needs to eat oats like me!" So, Tim took some oats from his breakfast and went outside.

Tim put the oats on the ground near the bird. The bird hopped closer and started to eat the oats. The bird began to feel better and stronger. Tim was very happy to help the bird. Then, Tim went back inside and shut the door. He knew that he and the bird would both grow strong by eating their oats.

John looked out the window. He gazed up at the bright, blue sky, feeling peaceful and content. Suddenly, something caught his eye.

When he looked closer, he saw a modern airplane flying by. John watched in awe as the airplane flew over the city. He couldn't believe his eyes.

Just then, John's mother walked in. She saw the excitement on her son's face and asked him what he was looking at. John told his mother about the airplane and she smiled at him.

"Would you like to travel one day, John?" she asked. He enthusiastically said yes.

John smiled as he watched the airplane fly away. His mother told him that if he worked hard and believed in himself, anything was possible.

John learned an important lesson that day: follow your dreams and never give up. He never stopped gazing up and wondering what else he could achieve.
Write a short story.

Lily liked to spin. She spun in her dress, she spun with her toys, she spun on the grass. She spun so fast that she felt dizzy and happy. She liked to spin with her friends, too.

One day, she went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw a big round thing that could spin. It was a merry-go-round. She wanted to try it. She ran to it and climbed on. She found a horse to sit on. She waited for it to spin.

But it did not spin. It was broken. Lily was sad. She wanted to spin on the horse. She asked her mom and dad why it did not spin. They said they did not know. They said they were sorry. They said they could find something else to spin on.

Lily was patient. She did not cry. She did not yell. She did not get off the horse. She hoped it would spin soon. She looked around and saw other things in the park. She saw swings, slides, seesaws, and sand. She saw other kids playing and having fun. She smiled.

Then she heard a noise. It was a click. The merry-go-round started to spin. Lily was happy. She held on to the horse. She felt the wind in her hair. She saw the colors blur. She laughed. She spun and spun and spun. It was perfect. She liked to spin.

Lisa loved her grandma very much. Grandma lived far away, but she always called Lisa on the phone and told her stories. Sometimes, grandma also sent Lisa pictures and gifts in the mail. Lisa liked to look at the pictures and remember the fun times they had together.

One day, Lisa got a big envelope from grandma. She opened it and found a book inside. The book had many pages with photos and words. Lisa asked her mom to read it to her. Mom said, "This is a memory book. Grandma made it for you. It has all the memories of her life and your family. She wants you to know how much she loves you and how proud she is of you."

Lisa looked at the book and saw grandma's face smiling at her. She saw pictures of grandma when she was young, when she got married, when she had Lisa's mom, and when she met Lisa for the first time. She also saw pictures of Lisa's cousins, aunts, uncles, and grandpa. Lisa felt happy and sad at the same time. She said, "I miss grandma. I wish I could hug her and thank her for the book."

Mom hugged Lisa and said, "I miss her too, honey. But we can still talk to her on the phone and tell her how we feel. And we can send her a card and a drawing to show her how much we appreciate her gift. Grandma is very compassionate. She always thinks of others and tries to make them happy. She is a very special person and we are lucky to have her in our lives."

Lisa nodded and said, "Yes, mom. Grandma is very special. I love her very much. Can we call her now and tell her that?" Mom smiled and said, "Of course, sweetie. Let's do that." They picked up the phone and dialed grandma's number. Lisa couldn't wait to hear grandma's voice and share her joy with her.

Billy was playing in the kitchen. He heard his little sister crying. He felt sad. Every day, his sister wanted cereal. She wanted the biggest box of cereal she could find. 
Billy asked his Mom, "Can I get her a big box of cereal, please?" 
His Mom replied, "No, you don't have enough money. But you can try to find something else she can eat." 
Billy thought for a minute and then he got an idea. He knew he had some money hidden under his pillow. He ran quickly to his room and grabbed the money. Billy ran back to the kitchen and found a big box of cereal. He gave it to his little sister. 
The bright colors of the cereal box made her smile. She was so happy. From that day onward, Billy knew that he could always find a way to solve problems, if he thought hard enough.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a big, bossy brother named Tom. Tom liked to tell Lucy what to do all the time. Lucy did not like it when Tom was bossy.

One day, Lucy found a big piece of cardboard. She wanted to make a house for her toys. She cut it and used colors to paint it. Lucy was very happy with her cardboard house. But Tom came and said, "You can't play with that. It's mine!" Lucy was sad.

Lucy did not want Tom to disturb her. So, she found a quiet place in the yard to play with her cardboard house. Tom saw her playing and felt bad. He said, "I'm sorry, Lucy. You can play with the cardboard house." Lucy smiled and let Tom play with her. They played together and had lots of fun.

Anna and Ben like to play in the park. They have a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. But they also like to explore the woods behind the park. Sometimes they find bugs, flowers and sticks there.

Yesterday, they asked their mom if they could go to the woods. Mom said yes, but only if they stayed close to the park and came back soon. She said the woods were not very safe and they had to be careful. She gave them a snack and a bottle of water and told them to have fun.

Anna and Ben were happy. They ran to the woods and looked for new things. They saw a squirrel, a bird and a spider. They picked some berries and some leaves. They made a fort with some branches and some rocks. They ate their snack and drank their water.

But then they heard a loud noise. It sounded like a big dog barking. They got scared and ran back to the park. They saw mom waiting for them on a bench. She hugged them and asked them what happened. They told her about the noise and the dog. Mom said it was probably a coyote and they were lucky to get away. She said they were not allowed to go to the woods anymore. She said it was too dangerous and they could get hurt.

Anna and Ben felt sorry. They liked the woods and they did not want to stop exploring. But they also loved mom and they did not want to make her worry. They said they were sorry and they would not go to the woods again. Mom said she was proud of them and she loved them. She said they could still play in the park and have fun. She said the park was safe and there were many things to do. She took them to the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They smiled and played. They had a lot of fun.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together. Today, they want to wear costumes and dance. Lily has a pink dress and a crown. Ben has a cape and a mask. They put on their costumes and look at each other.

"You look like a princess!" Ben says.

"You look like a superhero!" Lily says.

They smile and hold hands. They go to the living room, where the music is playing. The door is open, so they can see the garden. They see flowers, birds and butterflies. They feel happy.

They start to dance. They jump, spin and clap. They make funny noises and faces. They laugh and have fun. They dance until they are tired. Then they sit on the sofa and drink some juice.

"That was a good dance!" Lily says.

"Yes, it was!" Ben says.

They hug and say thank you. They are good friends. They like to wear costumes and dance.

Tim and Lily are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a red rocket in the park. It is big and shiny.

"Wow, look at this rocket!" Tim says. "Can we play with it?"

"Yes, let's do it!" Lily says. "Maybe it can fly to the moon!"

They take the rocket to a hill. They put it on the ground and push a button. The rocket makes a loud noise and smoke. It starts to move.

"Yay, it works!" Tim says. "Let's go with it!"

They run after the rocket. They want to get inside. But the rocket is too fast. It goes up and up and up. It flies away from the hill.

"Wait, come back!" Lily says. "We want to go with you!"

But the rocket does not hear them. It goes higher and higher. It leaves the park. It leaves the town. It leaves the earth.

Tim and Lily are sad. They cry. They lost their rocket. They lost their chance to go to the moon. They do not know where the rocket is going. They do not know if they will ever see it again. They wish they did not play with it. They wish they left it in the park. They wish they had a different toy.
